title: Postpartum Exercise NZ
meta_desc: Return to the gym safely after having a baby in NZ. Learn about postpartum recovery, pelvic floor health, and find gyms with crèche facilities.
intro: After giving birth, it's essential to allow your body time to recover before returning to exercise. The New Zealand Ministry of Health recommends waiting at least six weeks before starting any strenuous activity. According to research, a gradual return to exercise can help prevent complications and promote overall well-being. Exercise NZ's subsidised gym scheme can also help make fitness more affordable, with discounts of 40-70% off gym memberships.

sections.heading: Postpartum Recovery Timeline
sections.body: The postpartum recovery period is typically divided into several stages. The initial six weeks are crucial for allowing the body to heal from childbirth. During this time, it's recommended to focus on gentle exercises like pelvic floor contractions and deep breathing. After six weeks, women can gradually introduce low-impact activities like walking or yoga. Research suggests that a well-structured exercise programme can help reduce the risk of postpartum depression and anxiety. The World Health Organisation recommends at least 150 minutes of moderate-intensity aerobic exercise per week for adults, including new mothers.
list: Wait at least six weeks before starting strenuous exercise
Focus on gentle exercises like pelvic floor contractions and deep breathing
Gradually introduce low-impact activities like walking or yoga after six weeks

sections.heading: Pelvic Floor Health
sections.body: The pelvic floor muscles play a vital role in supporting the bladder, uterus, and bowels. During pregnancy and childbirth, these muscles can become weakened, leading to issues like incontinence. Exercises like Kegels can help strengthen the pelvic floor muscles. It's essential to consult with a healthcare professional before starting any new exercise programme, especially after giving birth. They can provide guidance on how to perform pelvic floor exercises correctly and safely. According to the Continence NZ organisation, approximately 1 in 4 women experience some form of incontinence, highlighting the importance of prioritising pelvic floor health.
list: Consult with a healthcare professional before starting any new exercise programme
Perform pelvic floor exercises like Kegels to strengthen the muscles
Prioritise pelvic floor health to reduce the risk of incontinence

sections.heading: Gyms with Crèche Facilities
sections.body: Many gyms in New Zealand offer crèche facilities, allowing parents to exercise while their children are being cared for. The YMCA and Les Mills are two popular gym chains that offer crèche services. Contours is another option that provides gentle exercise classes specifically designed for new mothers. These classes focus on low-impact activities like yoga and Pilates, helping women to gradually regain their strength and fitness. Exercise NZ's subsidised gym scheme can help make these options more affordable, with discounts of 40-70% off gym memberships.

sections.heading: Taking the First Step
sections.body: Returning to exercise after having a baby can seem daunting, but with the right guidance and support, it can be a safe and enjoyable experience. By prioritising postpartum recovery, pelvic floor health, and finding a gym that meets your needs, you can take the first step towards regaining your fitness and well-being. Remember to consult with a healthcare professional before starting any new exercise programme and take advantage of Exercise NZ's subsidised gym scheme to make fitness more affordable.
